newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-GRAF BLOCKS OUT DOUBTS, DISTRACTIONS TO DOMINATE SELES.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAF BLOCKS OUT DOUBTS, DISTRACTIONS TO DOMINATE SELES.

text.p: A championship was on the line Sunday, so Steffi Graf blocked out all the distractions and doubts and played one of her most dominant matches ever to claim another Grand Slam crown.

Graf, who had struggled to find her game and maintain her focus during the fortnight, put it all together on Stadium Court to beat Monica Seles 7-5 6-4 and move one step closer to the undisputed title of all-time greatest women's player.

"I felt so nervous before the match and I felt like I had an upset stomach and I was really nervous," Graf admitted after successfully defending her title in her 29th appearance in a Grand Slam final.
"I haven't really played very well during the tournament and, you know, you are playing Monica in the finals. If that is not an occasion to get nervous, then I don't know when."
Once on court, the safe haven from the personal hell she has lived through for more than a year, Graf loosened up and geared up for what she does best -- win.
"I didn't expect to be able to show that kind of tennis today and that is why I am so excited about it," she said.

For 13 months, Graf has lived under the dark cloud of her father's imprisonment in Germany. A month before the last Open, Peter Graf was jailed on suspicion of evading taxes in managing his daughter's massive tennis earnings.
In the middle of this tournament, Peter Graf's trial began. He is charged with failing to pay some $13 million in taxes and faces up to 10 years in prison.

Graf, who has been accused in court testimony by a former family accountant of knowing all about the financial dealings, has steadfastly refused to comment on the matter but her forlorn expression speaks volumes.
"It was really, really difficult to play this tournament," Graf said. "Last year was extremely difficult. This year was not any easier.
"I was really struggling during the tournament just to stay focused and to concentrate and that is why to be sitting here in this kind of position is incredible."
The 27-year-old Graf's position at the top of women's tennis is unassailable.
The Open victory was Graf's fifth and raised her Grand Slam total to 21 -- just three titles shy of Australian Margaret Smith Court's all-time leading 24, which includes 11 Australian Open crowns.
Yet Graf's coach, Heinz Gunthardt, was not confident about his star pupil's chances at this year's Open.
"This is probably the most difficult working conditions I've had," he said, referring to the personal distractions that plagued Graf in her preparation.
"Normally (when) I walk out there, she is concentrating first point to the last in a practice session of an hour and a half.

"This time around, when I met her in L.A. (two weeks before the Open), my God, I was very surprised how poorly she was hitting the ball, concentrating. It was really like, wow, what happened?" said Gunthardt, who had last seen Graf at Wimbledon.

He wasn't sure she could have survived a stiff challenge in an early match here. "If she had a really tough one early on I'm not sure. She wasn't playing well. Let's face it, she wasn't ready to play."
Graf was more than ready for Seles. She overwhelmed her co-world number one with her serving and dominated with powerful, flowing groundstrokes from the baseline.
Gunthardt rated it one of Graf's top performances.
Seles agreed.
"I think Steffi played the key points much better today," said Seles, who said she took painkillers for her shoulder but would not pin her defeat on injury.
"But I think the key was her serve, that she just kept getting her first serve in. I had no chance of returning it."

"I think her record speaks for itself," she added. "She's constantly winning Grand Slam tournaments. She is a great player and great athlete. When you have that combination, it is tough to play against."

Graf won her third Slam of the season, only missing the Australian Open, which Seles won and Graf skipped to recover from foot surgery. Graf also won the last three Slams of 1995 after missing the Australian because of injury.
Graf resists comparisons to other legends of the game.

"To have played the last six Grand Slams and win all six of them is an incredible achievment," conceded Graf, who said she would probably head to Germany after taking a few days off. "I'm not looking past that."
But tennis fans can still look forward to seeing Graf work her amazing magic on the court.
"To be able to play that kind of tennis and to get these feelings after the match, only tennis can produce that," Graf said. "And that is why I still love the game so much."
